exposure: Performance of Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) in the home environment
outcome: Child posture (sitting position, neck and trunk asymmetry, elevated arms and shoulders, inadequate upper-limb posture, ankle position)
Caregiver posture (trunk and neck asymmetry, upper-limb support, knee flexion)
cohort: Nine children with Congenital Zika Syndrome (mean age 36.77 ± 2.94 months) and their nine caregivers (mean age 27 years) from Campina Grande (PB), Brazil, were assessed.
finding: Children with CZS and their caregivers exhibit inadequate postures during Activities of Daily Living in the home environment, which may pose health risks.
cross-section timing: Data was collected when children were a mean age of 36.77 ± 2.94 months and caregivers a mean age of 27 years, during the performance of ADLs.
